derivation: [all-false-decides-type-reference; validate AUTHORITY_DEFINITION] One condition predicate ALL[BOOLEAN false, type fault, reference fault]; the leading false branch already decides the value, so both faults sit in unused branches. AUTHORITY-CHECKS Static definition admission: static literal types and all operand compatibility are checked even if another branch determines the predicate; AUTH-001: all branches are type-checked, including false or unused branches. AGG-003: COMPARE accepts equal INTEGER or DECIMAL types, so COMPARE over IDENTITY beneficiary and an IDENTITY literal is a type fault (AGGREGATES dynamic matrix: qualifier operand types are TYPE_INVALID). AUTHORITY-CHECKS Record and time admission: unknown type references are REFERENCE_INVALID. The reference-fault EQUAL compares two literals with the same undeclared type_ref, so its operand types are nominally equal and its only fault is the unknown reference. AUTHORITY-CHECKS Deterministic refusal selection: phase order governs before within-phase code order; directly checkable failures are accumulated within the phase and loop order cannot choose a different result. TYPE_INVALID is a phase-1 code; REFERENCE_INVALID is a phase-2 code, and type-reference resolution is deferred to phase 2 to distinguish a missing declaration from a malformed known value. Phase 1 already has a directly checkable TYPE_INVALID failure, so phase 1 is the first failing phase and the refusal is TYPE_INVALID regardless of row order, operand order or connective. For validate the refusal uses the PROTOCOL shapeRefusal {status,code,path:""}. For evaluate AUTHORITY-CHECKS gives {status,code,path:"",reasons,failed_checks}; reasons are empty for every code except AUTHORITY_NOT_ESTABLISHED and failed_checks is empty for every other code. Every source, class, envelope, proposal, operation, root, capacity and act digest is rebound after the mutation. Expected judgment derived from the specification text before any consumer execution.
